limitations: Extraction is an automated inventory, not a faculty-validated curriculum transcription.
Published summary counts can disagree with detailed tables; discrepancies and conflicting duplicate codes remain explicit.
Descriptions preserve full extracted competency cells and page continuations; PDF font spacing and table artifacts may require manual review.

NMC clarification amendments are explicitly applied, with original text retained. Disability competencies were under review in that clarification; no claim that these two PDFs alone capture every subsequent amendment.
All initial competencies are unmapped gaps. Only explicit source-record mappings can change relevance labels; keyword overlap never proves coverage.
No qualified medical faculty review, clinical mastery assessment, treatment-guideline validation, or clinical accuracy score was performed.
Source candidates are license research, not proof that text has been acquired or fulfills an MBBS competency. NC and SA requirements constrain reuse.
No accounts, paid services, copyright agreements, gated images, or communications with publishers were used.

source_observations.subject: Paediatrics
source_observations.observation: Detailed pediatric tables contain complete numeric sequences PE1 through PE32 (253 codes); page 350 ends PE32.1 and page 351 begins Psychiatry. The same source lists 35 topics and 406 competencies. This discrepancy is unresolved and no rows or topics were invented.
